Hyattsville Crime Data Analysis

Analysis of Hyattsville City Police Department annual statistics, 2015–2025. See data/notes.md for source-document errors, revised figures and gaps before quoting any number.

Setup

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

totals <- read_csv("data/totals.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

Total crimes per year

Citywide totals (crimes against persons + crimes against property), each year’s figure taken from its own report.

citywide_totals <- totals |>
  filter(geography == "citywide", measure == "total") |>
  select(year, count)

citywide_totals
ggplot(citywide_totals, aes(x = year, y = count)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2025) +
  # Start the y-axis at zero.
  # - By default, ggplot fits a line chart's y-axis to the data range. Here
  #   that would run from about 790 to 1,290, which makes the year-to-year
  #   swings look much bigger than they are (the 2021 low would look close
  #   to zero).
  # - limits = c(0, NA) pins the bottom of the axis at 0. NA tells ggplot to
  #   keep calculating the top from the data, so the axis still reaches past
  #   the 2019 peak of 1,288.
  # - expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)) adds no padding below zero, so
  #   the axis begins exactly at 0, and adds 8% headroom above the highest
  #   point so the peak isn't pressed against the top of the panel.
  # - labels = comma formats the tick labels with thousands separators
  #   (1,000 rather than 1000).
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1500),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)),
    labels = comma
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Total reported crimes in Hyattsville, 2015–2025",
    subtitle = "Crimes against persons plus crimes against property, citywide",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Total crimes",
    caption = "Source: Hyattsville City Police Department annual statistics reports"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#52514e", hjust = 0)
  )

Notes on these figures

  • The 2024 total is 910 in the 2024 report but 911 in the 2025 report’s prior-year column (theft revised from 464 to 465). The chart uses 910.
  • The 2023 spike coincides with stolen vehicles jumping to 314. Whether offense definitions or the records system changed is an open question for HCPD.

Comparing crime totals per ward

ward_totals <- totals |> 
  filter (str_detect(geography, "ward"), measure == "total") |> 
  select(year, geography, count)

ward_totals
NA
NA

ggplot(ward_totals, aes(x = year, y = count, color = factor(geography))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2025) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Crime totals per ward",
    color = "Ward",
    title = "Total crimes",
    caption = "Source: Hyattsville City Police Department annual statistics reports"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
